title: Full faithfulness of the canonical Galois stalk functor
statement: Let $K,K_s,\Omega$ be fields in $\mathrm{Type}\,u$, with compatible algebra structures $K\to K_s\to\Omega$, $K_s$ a separable closure of $K$ [def-pd-separable-closure], and $\Omega$ algebraically closed. Let $J$ be the small etale topology on $\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], let $p$ be the point defined by $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}K$, and let $p^*$ be its set-valued geometric stalk functor [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. Put $G=\operatorname{Gal}(K_s/K)$ with the Krull topology and $w=\max(u+1,v)$. Let $U$ be the forgetful functor from discrete continuous $G$-sets in $\mathrm{Type}\,w$ to sets. Let $T:\operatorname{Sh}(J,\mathrm{Type}\,w)\to\operatorname{DiscreteContAction}(\mathrm{Type}\,w,G)$ be a functor, and $j:T\circ U\cong p^*$ a natural isomorphism satisfying the canonical germ formula. The canonical germ formula is: for a sheaf $F$, $g\in G$, a $K$-automorphism $\tau$ of $\Omega$ with $\tau\circ i=i\circ g$ for the embedding $i:K_s\to\Omega$, an etale $K$-scheme $X$, lifts $x,x^{\prime}:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ over $K$ with $x^{\prime}=x\circ\operatorname{Spec}\tau$, and $z\in F(X)$, $j_F(g\cdot j_F^{-1}(\operatorname{germ}_x z))=\operatorname{germ}_{x^{\prime}}z$. Then $T$ is full and faithful: its map on each hom-set is bijective.

proof.text: Let A be the subfield of Omega algebraic over K. Roots of polynomials over A remain algebraic over K, so A is an algebraic closure and contains Ks. Every lift to an etale K-scheme factors uniquely through Spec A, since its residue field is finite separable. The resulting natural bijections identify the pointed-neighbourhood diagrams, all stalks and germ maps. Restriction of automorphisms to A respects these identifications. Apply the invariant-section theorem at A and transfer it to Omega. Since all g extend to Omega and all germs have representatives, the assumed formula identifies the action transported by j with that of the invariant-section theorem.

For finite separable L inside Ks, identify sections over Spec L with the Gal(Ks/L)-invariants in T(F). These identifications commute with every K-embedding, by the embedding-compatibility clause of the invariant-section theorem. Decompose each etale K-scheme into its finite separable components; the sheaf condition identifies its sections with the product of those invariant sets. An equivariant map between stalks restricts to all these invariant sets. The embedding formulas make the resulting section maps natural and independent of the embeddings chosen for the components, producing a sheaf morphism.

Every germ is represented on one finite separable component, so the stalk map of this reconstructed sheaf morphism is the original equivariant map. Conversely the componentwise invariant-section bijections determine each section map from its stalk map. Naturality of j identifies this correspondence with T.map, giving surjectivity and injectivity on all hom-sets. Empty schemes contribute the empty product.
